STEP 1 - Vessel type: Flat square plate with rounded corners, a rim band, and no inner wall. It is a flat plate.

STEP 2 - Vessel size: The plate spans about 445 px across. A blackberry (2.2 cm) measures about 35 px, which gives roughly 16 px per cm, so the plate is about 28 cm wide. Square plates of 20-30 cm are typical, so I take 26 cm as the width (676 cm²).

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Scrambled egg (white): about 15% of the plate, 101 cm². It is a chunky mound with a peak near 3 cm and an average near 1.5 cm. Volume 150 ml × 0.8 g/ml = 120 g.
- Roasted sweet potato: about 8% of the plate, 54 cm², 1.5 cm thick. Volume 81 ml × 0.8 g/ml ≈ 65 g.
- Blackberries and raspberries: about 8% of the plate, 54 cm², roughly 1.5 cm deep. Volume 80 ml × 0.6 g/ml ≈ 50 g. Counting about 12 berries at 5-6 g each gives about 60 g, so I use 60 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: No base layer is visible beneath the items, so I add none.

STEP 5 - Energy:
- Scrambled egg: 120 g × 150 kcal/100 g = 180 kcal
- Sweet potato: 65 g × 100 kcal/100 g = 65 kcal
- Berries: 60 g × 45 kcal/100 g = 27 kcal
- Total: about 245 g and about 270 kcal
